general: Extract every entity of the supplied types. Return exact spans from the query. Leave other text unlabelled.
C1 Words for a nationality, people or language, such as "American", "British", "Swedish" or "Canadian", are never Country or Location; label them Other.
C2 Titles of films, TV series and stage shows are Other, never Album or Song: "Roman Holiday", "Titanic", "All About Eve", "Four Weddings and a Funeral".

C3 An award name runs through its whole category after "for" as one Award span: "Grammy Award for Best Female Pop Vocal Performance", "Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Comedy Series", "National Board of Review Award for Best Director".

classes.name: MusicalArtist
classes.description: Refers to an individual actively involved in the creation, performance, or production of music.
rules: MA1 If a person is a singer, composer, or songwriter, annotate them as a musical artist entity instead of a person entity

MA2 Every individual musician is MusicalArtist: singers, rappers, DJs, composers, producers, instrumentalists and band members, also when named by surname or stage name only: "Buck Dharma", "Ad-Rock", "Cobain", "Iommi".
MA3 Examples: "Elvis Costello", "Nas", "Madonna", "Debbie Gibson", "Tiffany".

classes.name: Country
rules: CO1 Examples: "U.S.", "United States", "United Kingdom", "Australia", "Germany".

classes.name: Event
classes.description: Refers to a music-related occurrence or happening, such as a concert, festival, or competition.
rules: EV1 An event span starts at its year: "1976 Cannes Film Festival", "1978 Commonwealth Games".
EV2 Examples: "2003 World Championships in Athletics", "Vocal Event of the Year", "World War II", "Saint Patrick 's Day", "the first wave of glam metal".

classes.name: MusicalInstrument
classes.description: Refers to a device or tool used to produce musical sounds, such as a piano, guitar, or drum.
rules: MI1 Examples: "piano accordion", "six-string guitar banjo", "guitar", "keyboard", "bass guitar".

classes.name: MusicGenre
classes.description: Refers to a distinct category or style of music, characterized by its unique characteristics, themes, and instrumentation.
rules: MG1 Include regional musics typical of a certain place.
MG2 A genre span keeps a following word music: "Soul music", "Tejano music", "house music".
MG3 Examples: "Hip hop music", "Pop music", "reggae", "Punk rock", "Celtic rock".

classes.name: Other
classes.description: Refers to named entities that are not included in any other category.
rules: OT1 Examples: "Irish-American", "European", "Les Troyens à Carthage", "Didon", "Énée".

classes.name: Song
classes.description: Refers to a distinct category or style of music, characterized by its unique characteristics, themes, and instrumentation.
rules: SO1 A Song is one song, single, track or composition, not a genre: "Hey Jude", "Black Hole Sun", "Radio Ga Ga".
SO2 A title that comes right after the word single, singles, hit or track is a Song: "Believe in Me", "And She Was".
SO3 Examples: "Is That Love", "Tempted", "Clubland", "New Lace Sleeves", "The Lunatics ( Have Taken Over the Asylum )".

classes.name: Organization
classes.description: Refers to a structured group, institution, company, or association.
rules: OR1 This category covers a diverse range of organizations, including businesses, non-profits, educational institutions, and government agencies.
OR2 Examples: "Recording Industry Association of America", "Billboard", "BBC News", "Academy of Country Music", "Country Music Association".

classes.name: Album
classes.description: Refers to a collection of songs or musical compositions released as a single package
rules: AL1 An Album is a whole record release (studio album, EP, live album, soundtrack or compilation). Titles listed with their years among an artist's releases, or called an album, EP or record, are Album: "Woodface", "Doggystyle", "Bitches Brew", "Our Little Secret".
AL2 Examples: "American Idiot", "Dookie", "Sun Ra Visits Planet Earth", "Interstellar Low Ways", "Super-Sonic Jazz".

classes.name: Band
classes.description: Refers to a distinct category or style of music, characterized by its unique characteristics, themes, and instrumentation.
rules: BA1 A Band is a named musical group, duo or act, not a genre: "Sister Sledge", "Autechre", "Loverboy", "Brooks and Dunn", "Pendulum", "Grinspoon", "Primus". Label it Band, not MusicalArtist or Person.
BA2 Examples: "Backstreet Boys", "Spice Girls", "NSYNC", "LFO", "O-Town".

classes.name: Location
classes.description: Refers to a specific geographical or structural location.
rules: LO1 This includes but is not limited to: places (e.g., parks, landmarks), bridges, cities, towns, villages, areas and other distinct regions.

LO2 Concert halls, theatres, arenas and opera houses are Location, also when the name is that of the opera company playing there: "Sydney Opera House", "Paris Opera", "Vienna State Opera", "Carnegie Hall".
LO3 Examples: "Europe", "Stade de France", "Paris", "Théâtre de la Ville", "Bay Area".

classes.name: Award
classes.description: Refers to a device or tool used to produce musical sounds, such as a piano, guitar, or drum.
rules: AW1 An Award is a prize or honour, not an instrument: "Brit Awards", "46th Academy Awards", "Country Music Association awards".
AW2 Examples: "Grammy Award", "Brit Awards", "MTV Video Music Award", "Academy Awards", "Grammy Award for Best Alternative Music Album".

classes.name: Person
classes.description: Refers to an individual's name that is not a musical artist.
rules: PE1 Person is only for people outside music, such as actors, film directors and crew, athletes, critics and politicians: "Gregory Peck", "George Lucas", "Evan Lysacek", "Richie Unterberger".
PE2 Examples: "Barney Bubbles", "Stéphane Lafarge", "Bubbles", "Wolf-Rüdiger Mühlmann", "Glen Campbell".
